text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocker(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Classmate(x, y) ::: x is a classmate of y.
Jump(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
Shoot(x) ::: x is shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y) → Blocker(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
Man(michael) ∧ ∀x (Man(x) ∧ Classmate(x, michael) → Taller(michael, x)) ::: Michael is a man who is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If person x is taller than person y, and person y is taller than person z, then x is taller than z.
Man(peter) ∧ Taller(peter, michael) ::: Peter is a man who is taller than Michael.
∀x (∀y (Blocker(x, y) ↔ ¬Jump(y)) ∧ ¬Blocker(x, windy)) ::: Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting. Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
∃y (Man(michael) ∧ Classmate(y, michael) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(michael, y) ∧ Taller(y, peter)) ::: Peter is shorter than a man in Michael's class.
